title: Monell v. Department of Social Services, 436 U.S. 658 (1978)
citation: Monell v. Dep't of Soc. Servs., 436 U.S. 658 (1978)
text: Local governing bodies are persons that can be sued directly under 42 U.S.C. § 1983 when execution of a municipal government's own policy or custom inflicts the constitutional injury complained of. A municipality cannot be held liable under section 1983 on a respondeat superior theory solely because it employs a tortfeasor; liability attaches only for the government's own official policy or custom.

title: Owen v. City of Independence, 445 U.S. 622 (1980)
citation: Owen v. City of Independence, 445 U.S. 622 (1980)
text: A municipality may not assert the good-faith qualified immunity that its officers enjoy as a defense to liability under 42 U.S.C. § 1983. There is no tradition of immunity for municipal corporations, and neither history nor policy supports a construction of section 1983 that would justify recognizing such a defense for local governments.

title: Monroe v. Pape, 365 U.S. 167 (1961)
text: Congress did not intend to bring municipal corporations within the ambit of the word person as used in 42 U.S.C. § 1983, and therefore a city is not a proper defendant in a section 1983 civil rights action. This holding regarding municipal personhood was later rejected.
